extensions.scope: worker/src/render.ts only. The whole system is one inline STYLE template literal in that file. The CLI's terminal table is deliberately undocumented.

field.purpose: The page behind everything, and the gap showing through between cards.

bar.purpose: The chrome strip, the readout strip, and each tally tile. One chassis step above the field.

surface.purpose: A card and every panel. Two chassis steps above the field.

line.purpose: The 1px border and hairline, the 2px section rule, the tally's 1px gaps, the scrollbar thumb, the rail's dead fallback, the underline under a card name.

text.purpose: Every primary string: the age readout, a tally count, a project name, a note, a section label.

dim.purpose: The chrome strip, tally labels, the age note, a card's meta and git lines, the drawer summary, commit subjects, provenance lines.

accent.purpose: The panel's own colour. The lit end of the recency rail, the branch name, a commit age in a log line, the drawn list markers, the drawer's plus and minus, the focus ring, the selection fill.

hot.purpose: Condition only: a stale snapshot's age and note, the suspect tag's fill, the inverted stage chip and flags on a suspect card, and that card's rail.
hot.measured: 5.7:1 on a card (#101a24) as a mark, 6.0:1 as text on the bar (#0c131b). Far enough from the accent in hue that the two never read as one scale.

on-hot.purpose: The only text colour that ever sits on an alarm fill.

chip.purpose: The tag fill: the stage chip, the flags, and inline code.

recency-rail.purpose: The 4px rail down each card's left edge (6px at single width), set by days since last commit: r0 under 1d, r1 under 3d, r2 under 7d, r3 under 30d, r4 under 90d, r5 beyond. Fixed steps, never computed from the current board. A card with no git or no commits keeps the line fallback, so a lost class reads as age unknown rather than fresh.
recency-rail.measured: The dim end (r5, #20383c) does not reach 3:1 against the card and is exempt because the same fact is printed as text in the card's meta line. If the rail ever becomes the sole channel for something, it has to be re-measured.

readout.purpose: The snapshot's age, and nothing else, on any surface. The largest element on every page.

tile-count.purpose: A stage count in the readout strip's tile row. Second largest thing on the page, by design.

title.purpose: A project name on the board, in the device UI face because a human wrote it.

title-single.purpose: The same name on that project's own page. The only size change in the ramp.

body.purpose: Panel prose. 14px/1.4 with tabular-nums set on the whole body so every column of ages lines up.

note.purpose: A project's note on a card. Rises to 0.95rem capped at 42rem on a project page.

headline.purpose: The two section labels, over a 2px line rule, with the count pushed right in dim.

tag.purpose: The suspect count tag under the readout. At most one per page.

strip.purpose: The housing strip: wordmark at 0.3em tracking, subtitle, host. Also the back link at 0.18em.

stamped.purpose: A card's head row: zero-padded number and stage chip.

meta.purpose: A card's meta line (age, time in stage, flags) and its git line.

micro.purpose: The stage chip, tally labels, the drawer summary, the next heading, project-page block headings.

log.purpose: The recent-commit log, age in accent in a fixed 2.6rem right-aligned column. 0.74rem on a project page.

extensions.shadowPolicy: There is no box-shadow anywhere in the file, not even an inset hairline, and no filter or blur. Depth is a three-step chassis tone stack (field, bar, surface) separated by 1px line borders. Do not add a shadow token.

motion.name: develop
motion.purpose: The only animation in the system. The board comes up once from opacity .4 with the rail starting at line, staggered 22ms per card index via an inline --i, inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference. Only the rail moves in colour, so every word is readable from the first frame.

motion.name: develop-duration
motion.purpose: The --develop custom property. The one duration token in the system.

motion.name: develop-stagger
motion.purpose: Per-card delay. Set inline because the board's length is data, not a constant.

extensions.transitionPolicy: Nothing on the page transitions. There is one animation and it runs once on load.

breakpoints.name: readout-split
breakpoints.purpose: The readout strip goes from stacked to age beside tally. Four tiles plus the age do not fit across 375px.

breakpoints.name: capped
breakpoints.purpose: The tally column is capped at 46rem so the tiles stop stretching.

narrative.overview:
This is a dark-field instrument panel, not a document. The page's job is to answer three questions as numbers before a single project name is read: how old is this snapshot, how much of the board is lying to you, and where does the mass sit. Those three answers are the readout strip across the top. Everything under it is detail, laid out as a field of small lit cards rather than a column of status paragraphs.

There is one scheme and it is lit. color-scheme: dark, no prefers-color-scheme branch, no light twin. The reason is recorded at the token block and is the strongest rule in the file: two palettes meant every colour had to be decided and re-checked twice, and that is exactly how the single saturated ink was silently lost in the light scheme on 2026-11-04 while the dark scheme looked perfect. An instrument has a lit face. There is no second palette to keep true.

Colour carries meaning and nothing else. The field, bar, surface and line tones are the chassis. One instrument colour (accent, #3ad6c4) carries recency on each card's left rail and marks the values the machine read (branch, commit age, list markers). One alarm (hot, #ff5a42) is reserved for a condition the data actually holds, and is far enough from the accent in hue that the two never read as one scale. On a board with nothing suspect and a fresh snapshot there is no alarm anywhere, and that is correct.
keyCharacteristics: One scheme, dark, with no light counterpart to keep in sync.
Recency is a four-pixel rail down a card's left edge on a fixed six-step ramp, never a ground tone and never computed from the current board.
Two meaning colours only: accent for recency and machine values, alarm for conditions.
Square corners everywhere. No border-radius anywhere in the system.
No shadows at all. Depth is the chassis tone stack: field, bar, surface.
Machine type (monospace) for every value the machine stamped; the device UI face for human text.
Every card states what is happening in one line, with its depth behind a plain <details>.
One motion in the system, and it is only the rail coming up.

rules.name: The One Scheme Rule
rules.body: There is one palette and it is the lit one. Do not add a prefers-color-scheme branch, a light twin, or a per-token light value. Two palettes mean every colour is decided twice and re-checked twice, and the second one silently rots: that is precisely how the saturated ink went missing from the light scheme on 2026-11-04. If a value needs changing there is exactly one place to change it.

rules.name: The Alarm Reports, It Never Emphasises
rules.body: hot is drawn only where the data holds a condition: a snapshot over a day old, a suspect card. It is never a heading colour, a brand colour, a link colour, or a way to wake up a region that looked flat.

rules.name: The Rail Has No Fresh Fallback Rule
rules.body: The rail defaults to the card's own border colour (var(--rail, var(--line))). A card that has lost its density class must read as "age unknown", never as "committed minutes ago". That is the one lie this page cannot tell, and it is why the fallback is the dead value rather than r0.

rules.name: The Dim End Is Exempt Because The Text Carries It
rules.body: r5 sits deliberately close to the card and does not reach 3:1 against it. This is allowed only because the rail is never the sole carrier: the same fact is printed as text ("23d") in that card's own meta line. If the rail ever becomes the only channel for something, it has to be re-measured before it ships.

rules.name: The Readout Outranks Everything Rule
rules.body: The snapshot age is set larger than the wordmark and larger than every project name, on every surface that exists, including a single project's page and every empty, missing and mismatch state. A reader who takes one fact away must take this one, because a dashboard that silently shows yesterday is the exact failure this product prevents. Never let another element outgrow it, and never render a surface without it.

rules.name: The Monospace Means Machine Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks what the machine stamped or the reader must type: ages, card numbers, stages, flags, branch names, counts, paths, commands. A project name and a note are human writing and stay in the UI face even though a terminal would set them in mono.

rules.name: The Counts Align Rule
rules.body: Tally tiles are column-reverse, count above label, so the row of counts can be read across without reading a single label. Any new tile joins that row rather than inventing its own stack order.

rules.name: The Readout Strip Is The Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: The page's main hierarchy move is the strip, not the cards: the three facts you can act on are answered as numbers at the top, and everything below is detail. A new fact that belongs to the whole board goes in the strip, and a new fact about one project goes on that card, never the reverse.

rules.name: The Row Flow Trade Rule
rules.body: The board is a row-flow grid, and the multicolumn layout it replaced read payload rank straight down each column. That property is genuinely lost: in row flow card 2 sits beside card 1 and the ranking zigzags. It was traded on purpose. Rank stays legible because every card prints its own zero-padded number, and a board that reads as one instrument at a glance was worth more than a ranking that survives a column break. If rank ever has to be exact again, this grid rule is the thing to revisit, not the card.

rules.name: The Cut Rule
rules.body: The board is cut into exactly two sections and the cut is a partition, never a re-sort: both sections keep payload order internally, and numbers are assigned before the split, so a card number always means the same rank it means in the terminal and moving a project between sections never renumbers it.

rules.name: The No Shadow Rule
rules.body: This system has no shadow vocabulary at all, not even an inset hairline. Separation is a tone step plus a 1px border. Do not introduce a shadow token to make a card "pop", and do not reach for an offset shadow: that is a different world's device, and this one is not that world.

rules.name: The Rail Is Not Elevation Rule
rules.body: A brighter rail means more recent, not nearer. Depth must never become a second channel for recency or for condition, and a suspect card is never raised, glowed or outlined: its chip inverts, its rail goes to alarm, and its flag prints as a word.

rules.name: The No Radius Rule
rules.body: Nothing in this system is rounded. A rounded corner reads as a soft content card, and the page is an instrument face made of panels.

rules.name: The One Lit Edge Rule
rules.body: A rectangle gets at most one coloured edge and it is the left one. Do not put the rail on another side, do not add a second coloured edge, and do not colour a card's remaining three borders.

dos: Do keep one palette. All colour decisions live in the single :root block and are made once.
Do keep the readout the largest element on every surface, larger than the wordmark and every project name, and never render a surface without it.
Do keep recency on the rail, on the fixed six-step ramp, computed from the last commit alone.
Do leave the rail's fallback at the dead line value, so a missing class reads as "age unknown".
Do keep accent for recency and machine-read values, and alarm for conditions the data holds.
Do give every condition a word. The suspect state ships on three channels and only one of them is colour.
Do state the alarm colour's measured contrast when a value moves: accent is 9.7:1 on a card, alarm is 5.7:1 on a card and 6.0:1 as text on the bar.
Do keep a card's face to one line about what is happening, with depth in the <details>.
Do use the CLI's exact flag strings so the terminal and the board never disagree.
Do check any new region at 375px before shipping it; that is the width the page is read at.
Do keep the whole system inline in render.ts: no framework, no build step, no client fetch, no external font. The page must work with nothing but the HTML that arrives.
donts: Don't add a prefers-color-scheme branch, a light palette, or a second value per token.
Don't introduce a third meaning colour, or use the alarm for emphasis, branding, a heading or a link.
Don't let the rail be the only carrier of a fact; if it ever is, re-measure it against the card first.
Don't compute the recency ramp from the current board, or reuse the rail to mean stage, priority or anything but recency.
Don't add a shadow of any kind. This system has no shadow vocabulary, and an offset shadow belongs to a world this one is not.
Don't put a coloured edge anywhere but the card's left side, or add a second one.
Don't mark a suspect card by raising, glowing or outlining it.
Don't add a second animation, add a transition, or let motion start from an invisible state.
Don't add script to the drawer, or to anything else. <details> is the mechanism.
Don't re-sort the payload, renumber cards after the section split, or make anything interactive beyond the project link and the drawer. The dashboard is read-only by product decision.
Don't interpolate a value into the markup without escapeHtml. That rule lives as a comment at the function.
